title: Credit quality fundamentals
facts: A high-quality credit demonstrates additionality (wouldn't happen without credit revenue), permanence (reversal risk managed via buffer pools), no leakage (emissions don't shift elsewhere), and robust MRV.
ICVCM's Core Carbon Principles (2023) are the leading quality benchmark; CCP-labelled methodologies signal integrity to buyers.
Avoidance/reduction credits (e.g. REDD+, cookstoves) trade at a discount to durable removals (DAC, biochar, mineralisation).

title: Registries and standards
facts: Verra's VCS is the largest voluntary registry by issuance; Gold Standard emphasises SDG co-benefits; others include ACR, CAR and Puro.earth (removals).
Every credit carries: registry ID, methodology, vintage year, project location, and verification body — retirement is recorded publicly on the registry.
Article 6.4 of the Paris Agreement is creating a UN-supervised international crediting mechanism alongside voluntary markets.

title: Blue carbon science
facts: Mangroves, seagrasses and tidal marshes sequester carbon per hectare at multiples of tropical forests, largely in sediment that stays stored for centuries if undisturbed.
Mangroves also deliver storm-surge protection and fisheries co-benefits, supporting premium pricing; Verra VM0033 is the main tidal-wetland methodology.
India's coastline (Sundarbans, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Andamans) hosts significant blue-carbon restoration potential.

title: Using credits in net-zero claims
facts: SBTi's Net-Zero Standard restricts credits to neutralising residual emissions (≤5–10%) at net-zero, not substituting for near-term abatement; interim use is 'beyond value chain mitigation'.
The mitigation hierarchy: reduce first, then remove, then offset — regulators (ACCC, CMA) have pursued greenwashing claims built on low-quality offsets.
IFRS S2 para 36(e) requires disclosing planned carbon-credit use: volume, type (reduction vs removal), registry and quality assumptions.

title: Case study — Microsoft removals portfolio
facts: Microsoft (carbon negative by 2030 pledge, 2020) runs the largest corporate durable-removals procurement programme — multi-year offtakes across DAC, BECCS, biochar and mineralisation, published in an annual sustainability report with contracted volumes.
Its RFP criteria (durability >100 years, additionality, verifiability) have become de-facto buyer standards for removals.

title: Plastic credits landscape
facts: Plastic credits (1 credit = 1 kg or 1 tonne collected/recycled, standard-dependent) run on Verra's Plastic Waste Reduction Program, PCX, and certifiers like CleanHub and rePurpose Global.
Quality hinges on chain-of-custody evidence and additionality versus existing municipal collection; social co-benefits (waste-picker formalisation) drive premiums.
Plastic credits are not carbon credits — they cannot support climate claims, only plastic-footprint claims.

title: Biodiversity credits (emerging)
facts: Biodiversity credit schemes (e.g. Terrasos habitat units in Colombia, Australia's Nature Repair Market from 2025) quantify ecosystem uplift per unit area and time.
Unlike carbon, there is no fungible global unit — buyers should treat biodiversity units as project-specific contributions, not offsets against harm.
Measurement typically combines species richness, habitat condition and threat-reduction indices, increasingly verified with eDNA and remote sensing.

title: India's carbon market (CCTS)
facts: India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (2023) transitions the PAT energy-efficiency scheme into a compliance carbon market with sectoral intensity targets, alongside a voluntary offset mechanism.
Obligated entities span energy-intensive sectors (steel, cement, aluminium, fertiliser); the Bureau of Energy Efficiency administers with CERC as market regulator.

title: Tokenised credits — cautions
facts: Tokenisation puts registry credits on-chain for fractional trade and transparent retirement, but registries (Verra 2022) banned tokenising retired credits after bridge schemes created zombie-credit risk.
Credible tokenised markets require live two-way registry bridges so on-chain retirement burns the underlying registry credit exactly once.

title: Price benchmarks by category
facts: Indicative voluntary-market ranges (2024–25): nature avoidance (REDD+) ~US$3–10/t, cookstoves ~US$5–15/t, ARR reforestation ~US$15–40/t, blue carbon premium ~US$20–40/t, durable removals US$100–600+/t.
Prices vary sharply with vintage, rating-agency scores (BeZero, Sylvera) and co-benefits — always quote a range, never a point price.
